sections.title: Player read-aloud
sections.body: The Custodian leans out, eyes glittering. “Oh my, you’re rather late. Come in, come in before the forms notice.”

sections.title: Scene summary
sections.body: The old faerie-like Custodian appears, mischievous and exhausted.

sections.title: Visible choices
items: Respect her process
Demand answers
Apologize for delay
Ask about the forms

sections.title: Player questions
items: What detail in The Whitefire Custodian tells you the official story is incomplete?
Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it?
What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?

sections.title: GM notes
items: Play her as sharp, old, fussy, kind, and done with everyone’s nonsense.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.
[ADD/SEED] "The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
[ADD/EARNED] The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder. (Instinct Medium 15)

sections.title: Clues
items: Custodian fatigue She needs help. The corporation monetized protection while starving maintenance. The person carrying the system is burning down.

sections.title: Loot
items: Tea, if accepted
Maintenance note
Permission to understand the Keystone
Whitefire Custodian's Ward-Charm: A small hand-carved wooden ratcoon mid-scamper has been thumb-worn smooth for luck. It is warm, and the forest feels a little kinder while you hold it.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Plot So Far: The party is in Act Four pressure: The old faerie-like Custodian appears, mischievous and exhausted.

Mechanics In Play: Use Daggerheart Duality Dice as baseline. Use the listed Difficulty and outcome options when a roll matters. Keep trivial actions no-roll; roll only when uncertainty, cost, or danger is interesting.

Roll Cards: s04-03-win-the-custodian's-trust S04-03 Win the Custodian's trust Win the Custodian's trust Presence Knowledge Presence Knowledge 12 Presence treats her as a person; Knowledge respects her craft. She becomes a service provider instead of an ally. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. She becomes a service provider instead of an ally. Use a...
Gm Fear Spends: Make neglected infrastructure answer at the wrong moment. Stress the Custodian's trust without turning her into a device.
Conditions Hazards: No official condition unless a feature, hazard, or fictional position calls for Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable.
Search Loot Clues: Hanging Office: Soul-Quiet Charm or Firstmoss if earned; failed ward splinters and dustless map as clues.
No Roll Guidance: Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.
Escalation: Escalate by making cost visible: time, noise, trust, ward instability, or someone vulnerable in danger.
Deescalation: De-escalate through respect, care, honest testimony, useful evidence, or a concrete concession.
Tv Mechanics Caption: Public cue: The Whitefire Custodian asks what the party does, what it costs, and who is protected.

Trait Variety Note: Primary traits in this scene: Instinct, Knowledge, Presence. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.

Class Community Ancestry Reveals: Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
